alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The pars nervosa and the infundibulum form the neurohypophysis, which is derived from nervous tissue. As such, this subdivision is pale staining compared with the regions of the adenohypophysis seen on the right side of this section.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The infundibulum is a part of the neurohypophysis and forms the stalk that connects the entire pituitary to the ventral surface of the brain. The infundibulum is continuous with the pars nervosa and consists of axons from hypothalamic neurons which eventually terminate in the pars nervosa.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These protein-filled spaces are remnants of the embryological structure called Rathke's pouch. Rathke's pouch is an evagination from the roof of the stomodeum and gives rise to all subdivisions of the adenohypophysis. The cells encompassing the cysts and located between these cysts and the pars nervosa comprise the pars intermedia.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Herring bodies are the expanded axon terminals of hypothalamic neurons. Herring bodies are most numerous in the pars nervosa and are eosinophilic with a granular appearance. They can vary in size, depending on the number of hormone-containing vesicles they contain. The nuclei adjacent to Herring bodies are those of pituicytes.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The zona reticularis is the innermost region of the adrenal cortex, positioned between the zona fasciculata and the adrenal medulla. The cells of the zona reticularis are arranged in branching rows, thus appearing like a network or reticulum.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Blood enters the adrenal gland through the capsule and percolates through the wide-diameter, fenestrated capillaries of the cortex. Steroid secretions of the cortical cells are released into these capillaries. Blood eventually exits the organ via veins located in the medulla.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In this horizontal section of the pituitary gland, the pars distalis is distinguished by its overall basophila compared with the pars nervosa above it. The pars intermedia occupies the region at the interface of these two major subdivisions. The pars distalis contains a mixture of basophils and acidophils, each with its distinctively staining secretory granules, not visible at this low magnification.
